ai_summary: Scottish wind generation is demonstrating strong clean energy performance, with an estimated 4.7 GW currently produced, representing 46.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity and contributing significantly to total GB wind output of 13.0 GW. This abundant renewable generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to the GB-wide intensity of 73 gCO2/kWh. However, structural cross-border transmission limits prevent this green power from reaching consumers further south. Through Balancing Mechanism turn-down bids, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 48.6 GWh, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £1,993,672. To replace this discarded zero-carbon electricity, thermal plants elsewhere burned an estimated 9,243,006 m³ of gas, needlessly emitting an additional 17,027 tonnes of CO2. Annualising today's constraint expenditure yields an estimated yearly curtailment cost of £728 million. Distributed across national electricity consumption, this network bottleneck adds an estimated £2 to £3/MWh to every electricity invoice in the UK, highlighting the urgent financial and environmental necessity of expanding grid export capacity.
